nodeData.note: Plant-parasitic nematodes are microscopic roundworms that feed on roots, causing weak, patchy crops that look thirsty or hungry. Organic farmers manage them with clean planting material, rotation, organic matter, antagonistic crops and biocontrol agents.

children.note: Nematodes are microscopic roundworms, mostly under 1–2 mm long. Soil holds huge numbers; most are helpful, and only some groups feed on plant roots.
Bacteria- and fungus-feeding nematodes and predators recycle nutrients in healthy soil. A nematode count alone does not mean a problem; the type matters.

manas.q: Are most soil nematodes harmful to crops?

children.note: Plant-parasitic nematodes have a needle-like mouth spear (stylet) to pierce root cells and suck their contents. Labs use it to tell them from free-living kinds.

manas.q: What mouthpart do plant-parasitic nematodes use to feed?

children.note: Eggs hatch into juveniles; the second-stage juvenile (J2) is the one that finds and enters roots. In warm soils several generations build up in one season.
Sedentary endoparasites settle inside the root (root-knot, cyst); migratory endoparasites tunnel through it (lesion, burrowing); ectoparasites feed from outside.
Plant-parasitic nematodes are estimated to cause around US$173 billion of crop damage a year worldwide, and warming may raise losses.
Four groups do most damage to farmers’ crops in the tropics and beyond.
The most damaging group for vegetables worldwide (M. incognita, M. javanica, M. arenaria). They attack hundreds of crops and thrive in warm, sandy soils.

manas.q: Which nematode genus causes root galls?

children.note: The J2 enters near the root tip and turns nearby cells into giant feeding cells; the root swells into a gall around the swollen, egg-laying female.
Globodera (potato cyst nematode) and Heterodera (soybean, cereals, beet). The female body hardens into a cyst full of eggs that can survive in soil for many years.

manas.q: Why are cyst nematodes so hard to eliminate from a field?

children.note: Migratory nematodes that tunnel through root tissue, leaving brown-black lesions; they attack cereals, banana, coffee, potato and legumes and open doors for root-rot fungi.
A migratory nematode of banana that destroys roots and corm surface, so plants topple, especially when carrying a heavy bunch. Spread mainly in infected suckers.

manas.q: What is the main sign of burrowing nematode in banana?

children.note: Nematode damage is often blamed on drought or poor soil because nothing is seen on the leaves except weak growth.
Weak, yellowish plants in round or oval patches that spread along rows and with cultivation.

manas.q: What field pattern points to nematodes?

children.note: Plants wilt at midday although the soil is moist, because the damaged roots cannot take up enough water.
Yellowing and poor response to fertilizer or manure, since sick roots cannot absorb nutrients.
Banana plants fall over with roots snapped off short, a classic burrowing nematode sign.
Nematode wounds let wilt fungi and bacteria in; Fusarium wilt and bacterial wilt are often worse where root-knot nematodes are present.
Dig up whole plants carefully, wash the roots and look – this is the quickest diagnosis.
Swellings of the root itself, from pinhead size to large knobbly masses; carrots fork and become hairy.
Tiny white, yellow or golden round bodies on potato or soybean roots, later turning brown – each is a female full of eggs.
Dark brown to black streaks and patches on roots (lesion and burrowing nematodes); in banana the corm and root surface shows red-purple to black rot when cut.
Few fine feeder roots and a pruned, bushy look as nematodes kill root tips.
Legume roots carry helpful Rhizobium nodules that are easy to confuse with root-knot galls. Mistaking one for the other leads to wrong action.

manas.q: How do you tell Rhizobium nodules from root-knot galls?

children.note: Nodules sit on the side of the root and rub off easily with a thumb; galls are swellings of the root itself and cannot be rubbed off.
Cut a nodule: an active one is pink to red inside. A gall is whitish or the same colour as the root, sometimes with tiny pearly females.

manas.q: What colour is the inside of an active Rhizobium nodule?

children.note: Nodules appear only on legumes (beans, peas, groundnut, soybean); galls can appear on almost any crop, including legumes.
A lab count tells you which nematodes are present and how many, so you can plan rotation or treatment.
Sample moist soil while a crop is growing or just after harvest, when numbers are highest; also before planting a valuable crop.
Walk a zigzag through one area and take 15–20 cores from the root zone (about 20–30 cm deep), including fine roots; mix into one sample.
Take one sample from weak patches and one from good areas so the lab can compare.
Seal in a plastic bag, keep cool and shaded, never dry or heat, and get it to the lab within a few days – dead nematodes cannot be counted.

manas.q: How should a nematode soil sample be stored before it reaches the lab?

children.note: Pull plants at the end of the crop and score roots from 0 (no galls) to 10 (fully galled) to track root-knot levels over seasons.
Fill pots with field soil and grow a susceptible tomato for a few weeks; galls on its roots show root-knot is present.
Keeping nematodes out is far cheaper than living with them.
Use nematode-free seedlings, tubers and suckers; tissue-culture banana plantlets start clean.

manas.q: Why are tissue-culture banana plantlets useful against nematodes?

children.note: Raise seedlings in solarised or otherwise clean media and never in soil from infested fields.
Wash soil off tools, boots and machinery before moving from infested to clean fields; avoid run-off water from infested plots.
Combine several methods; no single one wipes nematodes out. Synthetic nematicides are not allowed in organic certification.
Grow crops the local nematode cannot feed on for one or more seasons. Root-knot has a wide host range, so choose carefully (some grasses, cereals or resistant varieties).

manas.q: Why must rotation crops be chosen carefully against root-knot nematodes?

children.note: Some French and African marigolds release nematode-toxic compounds and are poor hosts; they work as a dense stand grown for 2–3 months, not as a few plants dotted in a crop.
A fast legume cover crop that is a poor host for root-knot, adds nitrogen and organic matter, and suppresses nematodes when turned in.
Brassicas like mustard release isothiocyanates when chopped and dug in moist soil. Field trials cut potato cyst nematode survival.

manas.q: What gas-like compounds make mustard biofumigation work?

children.note: Neem seed cake adds nematode-suppressing compounds plus nutrients and organic matter; widely used in India at planting.
Crab-shell meal, insect frass and similar chitin sources boost chitin-eating microbes that also attack nematode eggs; chitin products also act on nematodes directly.
Regular compost builds a varied soil food web with predators and parasites of nematodes, making soils more suppressive.
Microbes that infect, trap or repel nematodes. Best used as part of a programme with organic matter, not alone.
A fungus that parasitises nematode eggs and females; it reduced root-knot on eggplant in trials. It can rarely infect people with weak immunity, so wear a mask and gloves.

manas.q: Which nematode stage does Purpureocillium lilacinum mainly attack?

children.note: A soil fungus that parasitises root-knot and cyst nematode eggs, lives on roots and can trigger plant defences.
A soil bacterium used as seed or soil treatment that protects young roots against nematodes.
A bacterium whose spores stick to J2 juveniles and later fill the female with spores. Very host-specific and hard to mass-produce, but builds up in soil over years.

manas.q: How does Pasteuria penetrans attack root-knot nematodes?

children.note: Trichoderma attacks eggs and promotes root growth; nematode-trapping fungi (e.g. Arthrobotrys) catch juveniles in sticky nets – still mostly research.
Tomato varieties with the Mi gene resist root-knot, but resistance weakens in hot soils (above about 28 °C). Grafting onto resistant rootstocks protects tomato, eggplant and pepper.

manas.q: What weakens Mi-gene root-knot resistance in tomato?

children.note: Cover moist, tilled soil with clear plastic for 4–6 weeks in the hottest season; heat kills nematodes, weed seeds and pathogens in the upper soil.

children.topic: Banana suckers: paring and hot water
children.note: Pare off all roots and discoloured corm tissue, then dip suckers in hot water (about 53–55 °C for some 20 minutes) or briefly in boiling water before planting.

manas.q: How are banana suckers cleaned of nematodes before planting?

children.note: Do not use synthetic nematicides (not allowed in organic certification), move infested soil or plants, or rely on one method season after season.
Local priorities and rules.
Potato cyst nematode is a quarantine pest that now limits potato in highland areas; use KEPHIS-certified seed potato and long rotations. Root-knot is common in tomato and French beans.
Root-knot is a major problem in vegetables and protected cultivation; Purpureocillium and Pochonia biopesticides are registered with the CIB&RC, and neem cake is widely sold as an organic manure.
